html:
The Constitution of the United States is the supreme law of the United States. It was written at a convention in Philadelphia in the summer of 1787 and came into force in 1789. It is the oldest written national constitution still in use.

It replaced the Articles of Confederation, which had left the central government too weak to tax or keep order. Delegates met under the chairmanship of George Washington, with James Madison the leading thinker. Drawing on English law and Enlightenment writers such as John Locke and Montesquieu, they set up:

  • Three branches: Congress makes laws, the president carries them out, and the courts judge them, each able to check the others.
  • Federalism: power is shared between the national government and the states.
  • Compromises: a Senate with two members per state and a House by population; and the notorious rule counting an enslaved person as three fifths of a person for seats in the House.

The first ten amendments, the Bill of Rights, were added in 1791 to protect freedoms of speech, religion, the press and fair trial. Later amendments changed the country deeply: the 13th ended slavery after the Civil War, the 14th promised equal protection of the laws, and the 19th gave women the vote in 1920.

The Constitution has been amended only 27 times. It became a model for federal and written constitutions elsewhere, from Latin America to the Constitution of India, though most countries rewrite theirs far more often.
sum: The Constitution of the United States is the supreme law of the United States. It was written at a convention in Philadelphia in the summer of 1787 and came into force in 1789. It is the oldest written national constitution still in use.
